title: Cyclic orbit count for q-ary run sequences
summary: Count cyclically distinct q-ary sequences whose run distribution matches that of a q-ary maximum-length linear sequence.

formal_statement.body: For every source-admissible prime power $q$ and order $n$, define q-ary run sequences of period $q^n-1$ by requiring the source-proposed run distribution of a q-ary $m$-sequence. Determine and prove an exact formula for the number of these sequences modulo cyclic rotation.

scope.domain: q-ary pseudorandom run sequences used in shift-register and cryptographic sequence design
assumptions: The run types and distribution are the q-ary extension proposed by the source
scope.unresolved_remainder: The binary cyclic count derived in the source does not determine the q-ary extension. No inspected later result gives the exact orbit count for all admissible $(q,n)$.

citations.label: Kim--Song, run-sequence enumeration and distribution problems

progress.summary: The source proposes the q-ary run-sequence extension and explicitly identifies its cyclic enumeration as a difficult research problem.
